title: Small Faces
creator: Gillies MacKinnon
description: Director Gillies MacKinnon’s drama about three teenage brothers caught up in the street gangs of 1968 Glasgow. One wants to be an artist. A key scene plays out in Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, the red sandstone museum in the West End.

title: Ratcatcher
creator: Lynne Ramsay
description: Lynne Ramsay’s first feature: a boy in a tenement during the 1973 binmen’s strike, when rubbish piled up across the city. Slow and quiet. The canal at its centre is the Forth and Clyde, which runs through Maryhill in the north of the city.

title: Taggart
creator: Glenn Chandler
description: Writer Glenn Chandler’s Glasgow murder series ran for 27 years, set around Maryhill police station. “There’s been a murder” became a catchphrase. The Glasgow Necropolis, the Victorian hilltop cemetery behind the cathedral, was a favourite location.

title: Comfort and Joy
creator: Bill Forsyth
description: Director Bill Forsyth’s comedy about a radio DJ caught between rival ice-cream van firms. It came out just as Glasgow’s real ice-cream wars turned deadly: six of the Doyle family died in an arson attack on their Ruchazie flat in April 1984.

title: My Name Is Joe
creator: Ken Loach
description: Ken Loach’s drama about a recovering alcoholic coaching a boys’ football team and falling for a health visitor. Peter Mullan won Best Actor at Cannes. It was shot in Ruchill, a north Glasgow district, with local non-actors. The dialect is thick.

title: Still Game
creator: Ford Kiernan and Greg Hemphill
description: Ford Kiernan and Greg Hemphill’s sitcom about two pensioners, Jack and Victor, in a tower block in a fictional Glasgow scheme. It ran on and off until 2019. Live stage versions sold out the Hydro, the big arena by the Clyde, for weeks.

title: Red Road
creator: Andrea Arnold
place: Site of the Red Road flats
description: Andrea Arnold’s first feature. A CCTV operator watching the city on screens spots a man from her past. Much of it unfolds in the Red Road flats, once among Europe’s tallest housing blocks. They were demolished between 2012 and 2015.

title: Under the Skin
creator: Jonathan Glazer
description: Jonathan Glazer’s science-fiction film with Scarlett Johansson as an alien driving a van, picking up men. Many street scenes were shot with hidden cameras on real shoppers on Argyle Street, the city’s main shopping street. Strange and slow.
